lit: a great vessel is completed late

story.text: The phrase comes from the Daodejing, in a passage of paradoxes about the Way: the great square has no corners, the great vessel is completed late, the great sound is barely heard, the great image has no shape. Later readers took the great vessel that takes longest to finish as a picture of a person of great ability who succeeds late in life.

use.how: Predicate or after 是/可谓, said of a person whose success came late: 他是大器晚成。 Also used to encourage someone still waiting for success.

near.diff: 后起之秀 is a young newcomer who quickly outshines others; 大器晚成 is someone who succeeds only after many years.

cue: Your friend's father published his first novel at fifty-eight and it became a bestseller. How do you describe him?

ctx.s: 他四十多岁才出第一本书，真是{大器晚成}。
ctx.en: He only published his first book in his forties; a real late bloomer.

ctx.s: 别着急，有的人就是{大器晚成}，你的机会还在后头。
ctx.en: Don't worry, some people just bloom late; your chance is still ahead of you.

ctx.s: 这位画家年轻时默默无闻，六十岁以后才成名，可谓{大器晚成}。
ctx.en: The painter was unknown when young and only became famous after sixty; truly a late bloomer.

ctx.s: “我现在转行还来得及吗？”“当然，说不定你就是{大器晚成}的那种人。”
ctx.en: "Is it too late for me to change careers?" "Of course not; maybe you're the late-blooming type."

ctx.s: 奶奶常说，小时候不起眼的孩子，长大了也可能{大器晚成}。
ctx.en: Grandma always said that a child who seems ordinary may still turn out a late bloomer.

ctx.s: 媒体称这位三十五岁才首次夺冠的选手是{大器晚成}的典型。
ctx.en: The media called the player, who won his first title at thirty-five, a textbook late bloomer.

bad.s: 这座大桥{大器晚成}，比计划晚了两年才通车。
bad.en: (meant: the bridge was finished two years late)
bad.why: It praises a person whose talent is recognised late, not a project that runs behind schedule.

bad.s: 他做作业总是{大器晚成}，每次都最后一个交。
bad.en: (meant: he is always slow and hands in homework last)
bad.why: It is praise for late success in life, not a complaint about being slow or late with a task.

mean: getting better day by day (a business)
lit: rising like steam, higher every day

use.how: Predicate of a business, career, economy or organisation: 生意蒸蒸日上。 Common in good wishes: 祝事业蒸蒸日上。

near.diff: 日新月异 is rapid change, as in technology or a city's look; 蒸蒸日上 is steadily growing prosperity.

cue: A bakery that opened two years ago keeps getting more customers and has just opened a second shop. How is its business doing?

ctx.s: 他开的小饭馆生意{蒸蒸日上}。
ctx.en: The little restaurant he opened is doing better and better.

ctx.s: 自从换了新经理，公司的业绩{蒸蒸日上}。
ctx.en: Since the new manager came in, the company's results have been rising steadily.

ctx.s: 新年快乐，祝贵公司事业{蒸蒸日上}！
ctx.en: Happy New Year, and may your company go from strength to strength!

ctx.s: 这个小镇靠发展旅游业，经济{蒸蒸日上}。
ctx.en: By developing tourism, the town's economy is thriving more every year.

ctx.s: “最近店里怎么样？”“托您的福，{蒸蒸日上}！”
ctx.en: "How's the shop lately?" "Thanks to you, better every day!"

ctx.s: 几年前还濒临倒闭的工厂，如今一派{蒸蒸日上}的景象。
ctx.en: The factory that was close to closing a few years ago is now flourishing.

bad.s: 今天的气温{蒸蒸日上}，热得受不了。
bad.en: (meant: the temperature keeps rising today)
bad.why: Despite the steam image it is not about heat; it describes a business or career that keeps prospering.

bad.s: 最近城里的犯罪率{蒸蒸日上}。
bad.en: (meant: the crime rate keeps going up)
bad.why: It is praise for something flourishing; it cannot describe a bad thing increasing.

mean: built up bit by bit over time
lit: accumulated day by day, piled up month by month

use.how: Used alone as a clause, as an attribute (日积月累的经验) or with 下来; about knowledge, skill, habits or problems built up over a long time. It takes no object.

near.diff: 积少成多 stresses small amounts adding up to a lot; 日积月累 stresses the long stretch of time it takes.

cue: Your friend asks how you got so fluent. You say there was no trick: just a little every day for years.

ctx.s: 词汇量要靠{日积月累}，不能指望一天背完。
ctx.en: Vocabulary grows slowly over time; you can't expect to learn it all in one day.

ctx.s: 他的经验是多年{日积月累}下来的。
ctx.en: His experience was built up over many years.

ctx.s: 这些小毛病{日积月累}，最后变成了大问题。
ctx.en: These small faults piled up over time and finally became a big problem.

ctx.s: 河口的这片沙洲，是泥沙{日积月累}冲积而成的。
ctx.en: The sandbank at the river mouth was formed by silt laid down little by little over a very long time.

ctx.s: “你的字怎么写得这么好？”“没什么诀窍，就是十几年{日积月累}的功夫。”
ctx.en: "How is your handwriting so good?" "No secret, just the skill built up over more than ten years."

ctx.s: 两个人之间的矛盾是{日积月累}的，不是一次吵架造成的。
ctx.en: The tension between them built up over a long time; it wasn't caused by one argument.

bad.s: 我昨天一个晚上就{日积月累}了很多知识。
bad.en: (meant: I learned a lot in one evening)
bad.why: It means building up over months and years, so it contradicts a single evening.

bad.s: 我要{日积月累}钱，将来买房子。
bad.en: (meant: I want to save up money to buy a house)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; say you save little by little, or that the money was built up over time.

mean: a green newcomer, just starting out
lit: just come out of the thatched cottage

story.text: Liu Bei went three times to the thatched cottage where the young Zhuge Liang lived in retirement before Zhuge agreed to serve him. Soon after, Cao Cao's army attacked, and at Bowang Zhuge Liang laid an ambush with fire and routed it. The novel's verse calls this his first achievement on coming out of the thatched cottage, and the phrase came to mean anyone just starting out.

use.how: Attribute (初出茅庐的年轻人) or predicate, about a person new to a job, field or society; often modest when said of oneself.

near.diff: 乳臭未干 scornfully calls someone a mere child; 初出茅庐 neutrally says they are new and inexperienced.

cue: On his first day at a law firm, a fresh graduate tells the partners modestly that he knows he still has everything to learn.

ctx.s: 我刚毕业，{初出茅庐}，还有很多东西要学。
ctx.en: I've only just graduated and I'm brand new; I still have a lot to learn.

ctx.s: 别看他{初出茅庐}，这次的方案做得很漂亮。
ctx.en: He may be new, but he did a beautiful job on this proposal.

ctx.s: 那时候她还是个{初出茅庐}的小记者，什么都不懂。
ctx.en: Back then she was a green young reporter who knew nothing.

ctx.s: {初出茅庐}的年轻人难免犯错，多给他们一些机会吧。
ctx.en: Newcomers are bound to make mistakes; give them a few more chances.

ctx.s: “这个项目交给新人行吗？”“他虽然{初出茅庐}，但很肯学。”
ctx.en: "Can we give this project to a new hire?" "He's inexperienced, but he's eager to learn."

ctx.s: 这位导演{初出茅庐}，第一部作品就获了大奖。
ctx.en: The director was a complete newcomer, yet his very first film won a major award.

bad.s: 这款新手机{初出茅庐}，卖得很好。
bad.en: (meant: the new phone has just come out and sells well)
bad.why: It describes a person new to work or society, not a product that has just been released.

bad.s: 退休多年的老教练这次{初出茅庐}，再次带队参赛。
bad.en: (meant: the old coach came out of retirement)
bad.why: It means a beginner's first steps, not a veteran's return; a comeback calls for a different idiom.

mean: to gain new insight by reviewing the old
lit: to warm up the old and come to know the new

story.text: Confucius said: one who keeps reviewing what he has already learned and gains new understanding from it is fit to be a teacher. The saying became the classic Chinese statement that real learning comes from going back over old material, not only from adding more.

use.how: Predicate or advice, about studying, rereading books or looking back at history and finding something new in it: 读史可以温故知新。

near.diff: 熟能生巧 is practice turning into skill; 温故知新 is review turning into new understanding.

cue: Rereading a novel you studied at school, you notice things you never saw at sixteen.

ctx.s: 考试前把旧笔记再看一遍，可以{温故知新}。
ctx.en: Going over your old notes before the exam helps you see things afresh.

ctx.s: 这本书我读了三遍，每次都能{温故知新}。
ctx.en: I've read this book three times and find something new each time.

ctx.s: 老师常说：“学习要{温故知新}，不要学了新的就忘了旧的。”
ctx.en: The teacher often said: "Learn by reviewing the old to understand the new; don't forget the old as soon as you learn something new."

ctx.s: 重读历史，往往能{温故知新}，看清今天的问题。
ctx.en: Rereading history often brings new insight and helps us see today's problems clearly.

ctx.s: 教练经常带队员重看以前的比赛录像，{温故知新}，找出新的改进办法。
ctx.en: The coach often has the players rewatch old match videos, going back over the old to find new ways to improve.

ctx.s: 他退休后重新翻开大学课本，{温故知新}，竟有了不少新的体会。
ctx.en: After retiring he reopened his university textbooks and, to his surprise, gained many new insights.

bad.s: 我今天{温故知新}，学了一个全新的软件。
bad.en: (meant: today I learned something completely new)
bad.why: It requires going back over what you already know; learning brand-new material is not reviewing the old.

bad.s: 他很{温故知新}，总是怀念过去的日子。
bad.en: (meant: he is nostalgic)
bad.why: It is about learning, not nostalgia, and it cannot be modified by hen like an adjective.

mean: to infer the rest from a single example
lit: shown one, come back with three

story.text: Confucius described how he taught: he did not explain until a student was struggling to understand, and if he lifted up one corner of a subject and the student could not come back with the other three corners, he did not repeat the lesson. From this image of one corner of a square implying the other three comes the idiom.

use.how: Predicate, often after 能/要/学会, about applying one example or lesson to similar cases; in official language also 'apply a lesson to all similar cases'.

near.diff: 融会贯通 is integrating a whole field into full understanding; 举一反三 is extending one example to similar cases.

cue: Shown how to solve one kind of problem, a pupil solves five different variations of it without any help.

ctx.s: 这孩子很聪明，教他一道题，他就能{举一反三}。
ctx.en: This child is clever: teach him one problem and he can work out the rest.

ctx.s: 做数学题不要死记答案，要学会{举一反三}。
ctx.en: Don't memorise answers in maths; learn to apply one method to similar problems.

ctx.s: 老师讲完例题，让我们{举一反三}，自己做后面的练习。
ctx.en: After going through the example, the teacher had us apply it ourselves to the exercises that followed.

ctx.s: “这种新题型你怎么也会？”“跟上次那道差不多，{举一反三}嘛。”
ctx.en: "How can you do this new type of question?" "It's like the one last time; you just extend it."

ctx.s: 好的培训不是教会员工每一种情况，而是让他们能{举一反三}。
ctx.en: Good training doesn't cover every case; it teaches staff to work out new cases from what they know.

ctx.s: 这次事故提醒我们要{举一反三}，把其他工厂的安全隐患也查一遍。
ctx.en: This accident reminds us to apply its lesson widely and check the other factories for hazards too.

bad.s: 我{举一反三}了很多例子来说明我的观点。
bad.en: (meant: I gave many examples to support my point)
bad.why: Ju here does not mean 'give an example'; the idiom means working out many cases from one, and takes no object.

bad.s: 他说话总是{举一反三}，同一件事讲好几遍。
bad.en: (meant: he repeats himself)
bad.why: It praises the ability to generalise, not repeating something several times.

mean: to master a subject by pulling it all together
lit: to melt things together and run a thread through them

use.how: Predicate, often 把……融会贯通 or 做到融会贯通, about knowledge, theories or skills integrated into a deep, unified understanding.

near.diff: 举一反三 is extending one example to similar cases; 融会贯通 is joining a whole body of knowledge into one understanding.

cue: After years of separate courses in grammar, history and literature, a student suddenly sees how they all fit into one picture.

ctx.s: 学过的知识要{融会贯通}，才能真正用起来。
ctx.en: What you've learned has to come together as a whole before you can really use it.

ctx.s: 他把中西医的理论{融会贯通}，形成了自己的方法。
ctx.en: He brought Chinese and Western medical theory together into his own method.

ctx.s: 读了几十本历史书以后，她终于能把各个朝代的事{融会贯通}了。
ctx.en: After dozens of history books, she could finally connect all the dynasties into one picture.

ctx.s: “怎样才算真正学会一门语言？”“语法、词汇和发音都能{融会贯通}的时候。”
ctx.en: "When have you really learned a language?" "When grammar, vocabulary and pronunciation all work together for you."

ctx.s: 这门课的目的是让学生把前三年学的内容{融会贯通}。
ctx.en: This course aims to help students integrate everything from the first three years.

ctx.s: 老教授讲课从不看讲稿，对各派理论早已{融会贯通}。
ctx.en: The old professor never looks at notes; he has long since mastered every school of theory as one whole.

bad.s: 这两家公司{融会贯通}，合并成了一家。
bad.en: (meant: the two companies merged)
bad.why: It is about understanding knowledge as a whole, not organisations merging; just say they merged.

bad.s: 这条路{融会贯通}，可以直达机场。
bad.en: (meant: the road runs straight through to the airport)
bad.why: Running through here is mental, not physical; it describes mastering a subject, not a road connecting places.

mean: vast in scope and profound (a culture or field)
lit: broad and great, refined and deep

use.how: Predicate or noun phrase (……的博大精深) about a culture, language, body of thought or field of learning, never about a person.

near.diff: 见多识广 describes a person who has seen a lot; 博大精深 describes a culture or field that is vast and deep.

cue: After a year studying calligraphy, you realise each stroke has centuries of theory behind it and you have barely begun.

ctx.s: 中国文化{博大精深}，一辈子也学不完。
ctx.en: Chinese culture is so vast and deep you could never finish learning it in a lifetime.

ctx.s: 他越研究中医，越觉得它{博大精深}。
ctx.en: The more he studies Chinese medicine, the more profound he finds it.

ctx.s: “一个‘打’字有这么多用法？”“哈哈，汉语就是这么{博大精深}。”
ctx.en: "The word da has this many uses?" "Ha, that's how deep Chinese is."

ctx.s: 这部著作内容{博大精深}，值得反复阅读。
ctx.en: This work is vast and profound and deserves to be read again and again.

ctx.s: 茶道看似简单，其实{博大精深}。
ctx.en: The art of tea looks simple, but it is actually a vast and subtle field.

ctx.s: 参观完博物馆，外国游客纷纷感叹中华文明的{博大精深}。
ctx.en: After visiting the museum, the foreign visitors marvelled at the depth and breadth of Chinese civilisation.

bad.s: 我的老师{博大精深}，什么都懂。
bad.en: (meant: my teacher is very learned)
bad.why: It describes a culture or field, not a person; for a learned person use a different idiom.

bad.s: 这个房间{博大精深}，能住十个人。
bad.en: (meant: the room is very spacious)
bad.why: Great and deep are not physical size here; it praises the depth of a culture or body of knowledge.

use.how: Predicate or attribute about a person whose knowledge comes from wide experience and travel: 见多识广的老人。

near.diff: 博大精深 describes a culture or field; 见多识广 describes a person who has seen and experienced a lot.

cue: A retired sea captain who has sailed to fifty countries is never surprised by anything you tell him.

ctx.s: 我爷爷年轻时走过很多地方，{见多识广}。
ctx.en: My grandfather travelled to many places when he was young and has seen a lot of the world.

ctx.s: 你{见多识广}，帮我看看这块玉是真是假？
ctx.en: You've seen so much; can you tell me if this jade is real?

ctx.s: 当了二十年记者，她早已{见多识广}，什么场面都不怕。
ctx.en: After twenty years as a reporter she has seen it all and nothing fazes her.

ctx.s: “这种怪事你见过吗？”“我也算{见多识广}了，还真没见过。”
ctx.en: "Have you ever seen anything this strange?" "I've seen a lot, but never this."

ctx.s: 多出去旅行，人会变得{见多识广}。
ctx.en: Travel more and you'll become more worldly and knowledgeable.

ctx.s: 村里人遇到难事，都去请教那位{见多识广}的老船长。
ctx.en: When villagers face a problem, they all go to ask the worldly old captain.

bad.s: 这本书{见多识广}，内容很丰富。
bad.en: (meant: this book covers a lot)
bad.why: It describes a person's experience of the world, not a book's content; say the book's content is rich.

bad.s: 他视力很好，很远的东西也能{见多识广}。
bad.en: (meant: his eyesight is good and he can see far)
bad.why: Seeing here means life experience, not eyesight; the idiom is about knowledge gained from seeing the world.

lit: one's gaze is short and shallow

use.how: Predicate or attribute about a person or decision that ignores the future for present gain: 目光短浅的做法。 Not about eyesight.

near.diff: 井底之蛙 is a narrow view from limited experience of the world; 目光短浅 is failing to look ahead to the future.

cue: A company cuts all research spending just to make this quarter's profits look good. How would critics describe the decision?

ctx.s: 只顾眼前利益，不考虑以后，太{目光短浅}了。
ctx.en: Thinking only of immediate gain and not of the future is far too short-sighted.

ctx.s: 为了省钱砍掉培训经费，是一种{目光短浅}的做法。
ctx.en: Cutting the training budget to save money is a short-sighted move.

ctx.s: “他为了一点奖金就跳槽了。”“我觉得他有点{目光短浅}。”
ctx.en: "He changed jobs for a small bonus." "I think that was a bit short-sighted of him."

ctx.s: 当年嘲笑网购没有前途的人，现在看来实在是{目光短浅}。
ctx.en: Those who once laughed that online shopping had no future look truly short-sighted now.

ctx.s: 村民们当初{目光短浅}，砍光了山林卖钱，如今连水都不够用。
ctx.en: The villagers were short-sighted and cut down the forests for cash; now they don't even have enough water.

ctx.s: 父亲常提醒我：做人不能{目光短浅}，要看得远一点。
ctx.en: My father often reminded me not to be short-sighted, but to look further ahead.

bad.s: 我{目光短浅}，看不清黑板上的字。
bad.en: (meant: I'm near-sighted and can't read the board)
bad.why: It is about poor foresight, not eyesight; for eyes use the ordinary word for near-sighted.

bad.s: 他{目光短浅}，做事特别踏实。
bad.en: (meant: he focuses on practical things and works steadily)
bad.why: It is a criticism of ignoring the future, never praise for being down to earth.
